prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Access/refresh tokens loaded from persistent storage never have token_expiry_time computed, so is_token_valid() treats a stale, already-expired stored token as valid. That causes the proactive-refresh check to be skipped and the client falls through to a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent token refresh whenever the process restarts with an expired stored token. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Access/refresh tokens loaded from persistent storage never have token_expiry_time computed, so is_token_valid() treats a stale, already-expired stored token as valid. That causes the proactive-refresh check to be skipped and the client falls through to a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent token refresh whenever the process restarts with an expired stored token. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1784 fixes the root cause directly in _initialize by calling the existing context.update_token_expiry() when stored tokens are loaded, restoring the exact invariant the pre-existing proactive-refresh branch in async_auth_flow already depends on (this is explicitly confirmed by #2875's own added code comment, which names token_expiry_time-not-restored as the cause). It's a 4-line change plus a new expired_tokens test fixture. #2875 instead patches the symptom: it inserts a new 'Step 3.5' branch inside async_auth_flow's generator that re-attempts a refresh right before the full-reauth path, duplicating logic that would already execute correctly once token_expiry_time is restored, and it alters yield/return control flow in the shared auth-flow coroutine, which is a larger and riskier surface than #1784's isolated one-time initialization fix.

prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive substring/full-string matching to find auth-param fields, which could false-positive on values that merely contain the field name as a substring (or across quoted values containing commas). Both PRs replace this with proper tokenization that splits the header into individual auth-param tokens (comma-separated, quote-aware, backslash-escape-aware) before matching. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive substring/full-string matching to find auth-param fields, which could false-positive on values that merely contain the field name as a substring (or across quoted values containing commas). Both PRs replace this with proper tokenization that splits the header into individual auth-param tokens (comma-separated, quote-aware, backslash-escape-aware) before matching. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3041's parser is scheme-aware: it first splits the header into top-level comma segments, then explicitly walks segments to detect where a new auth-scheme (e.g. 'Bearer') begins (via space-partitioning each segment) before collecting only that scheme's params — this correctly isolates the Bearer challenge when a WWW-Authenticate header carries multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer error=invalid_token'). #3012's helper (`_iter_www_auth_params`) instead finds only the first space in the entire header and treats everything after it as one flat parameter list, with no logic to detect a second scheme token appearing later in a multi-challenge header, so it would misparse headers advertising more than one auth scheme. #3041's diff is also larger (two cooperating functions, ~88 lines) reflecting this extra segment/scheme-boundary handling versus #3012's single ~45-line generic splitter.

prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a process restart, OAuthContext.oauth_metadata (the authorization server's discovered endpoints, including token_endpoint) only ever lived in memory, so a cold-start token refresh has no endpoint to call, forcing either a failure or a full rediscovery/re-auth cycle on every restart. clusters.pick_reason: #3041's parser is scheme-aware: it first splits the header into top-level comma segments, then explicitly walks segments to detect where a new auth-scheme (e.g. 'Bearer') begins (via space-partitioning each segment) before collecting only that scheme's params — this correctly isolates the Bearer challenge when a WWW-Authenticate header carries multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer error=invalid_token'). #3012's helper (`_iter_www_auth_params`) instead finds only the first space in the entire header and treats everything after it as one flat parameter list, with no logic to detect a second scheme token appearing later in a multi-challenge header, so it would misparse headers advertising more than one auth scheme. #3041's diff is also larger (two cooperating functions, ~88 lines) reflecting this extra segment/scheme-boundary handling versus #3012's single ~45-line generic splitter.

clusters.pick_reason: #3041's parser is scheme-aware: it first splits the header into top-level comma segments, then explicitly walks segments to detect where a new auth-scheme (e.g. 'Bearer') begins (via space-partitioning each segment) before collecting only that scheme's params — this correctly isolates the Bearer challenge when a WWW-Authenticate header carries multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer error=invalid_token'). #3012's helper (`_iter_www_auth_params`) instead finds only the first space in the entire header and treats everything after it as one flat parameter list, with no logic to detect a second scheme token appearing later in a multi-challenge header, so it would misparse headers advertising more than one auth scheme. #3041's diff is also larger (two cooperating functions, ~88 lines) reflecting this extra segment/scheme-boundary handling versus #3012's single ~45-line generic splitter.

members.title: fix(auth): match complete WWW-Authenticate parameters
members.author: tarunag10
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3041: WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive substring/full-string matching to find auth-param fields, which could false-positive on values that merely contain the field name as a substring (or across quoted values containing commas). Both PRs replace this with proper tokenization that splits the header into individual auth-param tokens (comma-separated, quote-aware, backslash-escape-aware) before matching.
